faq.q: How does the 50/30/20 insight decide what's a need versus a want?
faq.a: Each category is pre-mapped to needs, wants or savings. Rent, groceries, utilities, mobile, transport, education, medical, EMI, insurance and family support count as needs; dining, shopping, entertainment, subscriptions and any custom category count as wants; the savings/investment category plus any leftover income count as savings. The Insights tab shows the percentage split as guidance, not financial advice.

faq.q: What's the difference between a transaction and a recurring item?
faq.a: A transaction is a one-off income or expense with a date, category, payment method and note. A recurring item (rent, EMI, a subscription) is saved separately with just a description, amount and category — then added to the currently selected month with one click via '+ this month', which creates a dated transaction marked (recurring).

faq.q: Where is my data stored and how do I move it?
faq.a: Everything saves automatically to your browser's local storage — no account. To move or back it up, use Export JSON (re-importable) or the Accountant ZIP, which bundles the JSON backup, a transactions CSV, a plain-text monthly summary with per-category totals, and a README. Importing a JSON backup replaces your current data, and the import only accepts JSON files this tool exported.

faq.q: Do budgets and charts cover all months or just one?
faq.a: You pick a month at the top and the dashboard, transactions, budgets and insights all apply to that month. Budgets are set per category per month, with bars turning amber at 80% and red at 100% of the limit. The bar chart shows the last six months of income versus expenses, and insights compare the selected month against the previous one.
